parsed.explanation: No trans-specific entry crime is documented, but combined regime is hostile: buggery law (up to 10 years) gives police a lever, transgender people are distinctively exposed, police harassment of trans women and documented failure to investigate or intervene in anti-LGBT violence show impunity, and if detained, recent evidence shows common severe prisoner-on-prisoner violence, isolation, 3x overcrowding and life-threatening conditions with no gender-recognition framework for accommodation. Pervasive public hostility and police inability to protect Pride reinforce severity after outing, despite insulated tourist bubbles.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented airport/border screening, marker treatment or entry refusal for trans visitors; unresolved in dossier.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport governs; absence of domestic gender recognition is a resident gap, not a documented visitor border exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2023 report: common severe violence against prisoners targeted for perceived LGBTQI+ identity, cells at 3x capacity, harsh life-threatening conditions; Jan 2023 lockup beating with scalding liquid; 2018 study: perceived gay/bisexual/trans prisoners isolated, no specialised housing.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented gender-identity accommodation, protection or remedy in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest on buggery/morality grounds therefore leads into documented targeted custodial violence and isolation.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented for visitor bathrooms, wards or venues; 2019 Pride blocked and police said they could not protect amid hysteria in one coastal city.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local official hostility and police withdrawal suggest facilities/events protection cannot be assumed.

care_services.exposure: 2023 LGBT survey documents transgender health-care exclusion for residents; no visitor medication, HRT import or emergency-care evidence documented.
care_services.interaction: Dossier itself says health-system barrier falls mainly on residents dependent on domestic system, not short-term visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Buggery punishable by up to 10 years' hard labour, confirmed criminalising consensual same-sex conduct; no anti-discrimination statute; police harassment of trans women documented; police leak details, fail to investigate LGBT violence including murder, and do not intervene.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No documented trans-specific protection; occasional entry bar of anti-gay pastor in 2018 is not a trans-visitor protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Sexuality statute is secondary per rubric, but documented police practice makes it a usable lever against visibly gender-nonconforming people.

minors_guardians.interaction: Constitutional bar on same-sex union recognition could affect travelling partners, but no minor-specific rule is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Transgender residents distinctively exposed; violence against trans people reported common but rarely reported; 2013 mob stabbing of gender-nonconforming 16-year-old unsolved/no arrests as of 2022 and police failed to investigate; 2006 vigilante/police ill-treatment; sustained hostile opinion, at least 60% oppose acceptance in 2023.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Tourist resort bubbles described as insulated with rare incidents; no reliable police protection documented, and 2019 police could not protect Pride.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostility plus documented impunity means an outed visitor cannot rely on police intervention; tourist insulation is partial, not a remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: 2013 packet: victims reluctant to report because police leak and fail to investigate; 2012 organisation reported few sought prison recourse; no later legislative change sourced after 2023.
remedies_unknowns.protection: No documented functioning remedy for trans visitors; petitions to regional commission are resident/activist litigation, not visitor relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertain border practice does not offset documented custody and impunity; absence of recent incidents after Jan 2023 is not evidence of safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower severity/frequency than 0.15: routine visitor arrests, months of pretrial beatings and systematic custody abuse as primary pathway are not documented here, and no credible capital pathway is shown. Similar in that remedies are illusory and custody is violent.

Similar to 0.25: birth/identity-blind custody with frequent assaults, slow/ineffective remedies and short-to-long imprisonment exposure without execution. Here overcrowding and 2023 targeted violence place it at the lower end of 0.25.

Materially below 0.35: 0.35 detention rarely becomes imprisonment and lethal force is not threatened, whereas here buggery carries 10 years, custody violence is recent and severe, and police impunity is documented.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: uncertain border exposure sits above documented trans-specific police harassment, pervasive hostile public opinion and a buggery statute that can be used against gender-nonconforming visitors, with no statutory discrimination protection. The decisive interaction is arrest-to-custody: no accommodation framework, isolated minority prisoners, common targeted severe violence and life-threatening overcrowding in 2023. Tourist bubbles and lack of documented visitor arrests mitigate slightly, but do not offset impunity or custodial severity. Adult alone and adult with minor face same documented regime; no minor-specific rule is documented.
